notes.olungereza: The ki- prefix names a language: Kiswahili, Kiingereza, Kifaransa.
notes.jibu: Plural: majibu. As a verb: Jibu! (answer!)

guidebook.intro: Swahili is the language of primary school in Tanzania and is taught across Kenya and Uganda. Here are the words for the classroom, and for asking when you’re lost.

tips.title: “Of” agrees too
body: “Of” is **-a** with the noun’s own prefix in front: **somo la hesabu** (a maths lesson), **kitabu cha Neema** (Neema’s book), **kalamu ya Emma** (Emma’s pen), **masomo ya leo** (today’s lessons).
You’ll see the same prefixes in “my”: **kitabu changu**, **kalamu yangu**, **somo langu**.

tips.title: I don’t: si-
body: To say “I don’t”, swap **nina-** for **si-** and change the last **-a** of the verb to **-i**: **ninaelewa** (I understand) becomes **sielewi** (I don’t understand), **ninajua** (I know) becomes **sijui** (I don’t know).
You already know one: **sina** (I don’t have). Both **Sielewi** and **Sijui** are worth knowing by heart.

culture.title: Mwalimu
body: Teachers are deeply respected. Pupils often stand to greet a teacher entering the room with **Shikamoo, mwalimu!** or a chorus of **Habari za asubuhi, mwalimu!**
